kill_argument: The only positive finding, a 95% interval that excludes zero, is decided by the cross-fitting seeds, not the data. The lower bound is $9.6 on an SE of $798 (p = 0.049). The five fixed repetitions taken alone give lower bounds of 55, 57, -20, -26 and -3 dollars: three of five would not exclude zero, and the between-repetition SD of 52 gives the averaged bound a Monte Carlo SD near 23, more than twice the margin. The fixed checks fall on both sides of zero (trim -80, parametric -88, covset (a) -183, OLS -28; forests +144, IPW +26), the relative-contrast interval includes zero, R2*_0 is 0.0011, and the placebo fails at -1,543, as large as the estimate. A hostile referee reads this as: the data do not separate the contrast from zero, and the comparison is biased by about its own size. What I attacked and found holding: every claim value equals its run metric; the post-code-r1 code diff is F1-F4 only; each analysis ran once, in order, with no unlogged real-data run; no benchmark comparison exists; wording follows the H3 fail and the disagreement rule.

findings.text: The H1 decision sits inside cross-fitting noise, and the claims do not show it. main-aipw gives 1,573 (SE 798), 95% CI [9.6, 3,136], p = 0.049. The design fixed S = 5 repetitions with mean aggregation, and that rule is applied correctly. But the per-repetition estimates in runs/main-aipw/metrics.json (theta_rep0-4 = 1,597, 1,612, 1,522, 1,511, 1,621; se_rep0-4 = 786, 794, 787, 784, 828) give single-repetition lower bounds of +55, +57, -20, -26 and -3 (my arithmetic from the metrics, nothing re-run). Three of five would not exclude zero. The between-repetition SD is 52, so the averaged lower bound has a Monte Carlo SD of about 23 against a margin of 9.6, and a different seed base would flip H1 with roughly one chance in three. design.threats[9] promised that 'the per-repetition estimates and SEs are reported so split noise is visible', yet no claim carries theta_rep or se_rep. Claim h1-decision says only 'met ... by a margin of about ten dollars'. The macro \PrimaryCiLow prints '10'. The relative-contrast interval [-5.1%, 71.0%] includes zero, and h1-decision does not say so. Ruling: h1-decision is partly supported. The rule's outcome is right, but the sentence omits that the decision is unstable within the design's own fixed seeds.
findings.evidence: runs/main-aipw/metrics.json theta_rep0-4, se_rep0-4, ci_low, rel_ci_low_pct; claims.jsonl h1-decision, primary-ci-low; plan.json design.threats[9] and method.cross_fitting. Cheapest remedy, no new run and no change of rule or aggregation: (1) add result claims for theta_rep0-4 and se_rep0-4 from main-aipw. (2) Extend h1-decision: the lower bound is $9.6; three of the five repetitions taken alone give intervals that include zero, so the decision lies within cross-fitting noise; the relative-contrast interval includes zero. (3) The paper never calls the contrast 'significant' without that sentence. The primary estimate and the H1 rule stay as fixed.
findings.response: Fixed without a new run: claims primary-theta-rep0-4 and primary-se-rep0-4 copy main-aipw's logged metrics; h1-decision now says the lower bound is $9.6, three of five repetitions alone give intervals including zero (decision within cross-fitting noise), the relative-contrast interval includes zero, and 'significant' is never used without that sentence.

findings.text: Claim sens-reading calls black 'the strongest robust group'. The robust verdicts for black, married and nodegree are artifacts of the benchmark measure, not evidence. code/sens_imbens.py benchmark_r2 sets R2_D(G) = max(0, (V - V_-G)/(V - V_-G + pi^2/3)), with V the variance of the fitted logit index over all 16,177 men. I checked this in scratch with treatment and covariates only (lalonde-reviewer4/vcheck.py; no outcome read). V = 13.0, which is 12.3 among CPS men and 4.2 among treated men, and the minimum index is -22. So V is driven by CPS men far below any treated man. Dropping black raises the index variance (V - V_-G = -1.45), and so does dropping nodegree (-0.83) or married (-0.04), so all three are floored at 0. Yet black is by far the strongest predictor of participation: dropping it lowers the log-likelihood by 179.3 (McFadden partial 0.30). The corresponding drops are 51.3 for age, 22.4 for earn74, 19.7 for married, 19.2 for earn75, 12.6 for educ, 7.3 for hisp and 2.7 for nodegree. The measure therefore scores race, the covariate with the largest imbalance (nd 1.72), as the weakest confounder. With t_0 = 9.6, any nonzero R2_D would probably make the black verdict 'not robust'. runs/NOTES.md already calls this 'mechanical'. The claim keeps 'strongest robust group is black' and qualifies it only with 'floored at zero', which a reader will take as 'robust to confounding as strong as race'. Ruling: sens-reading is partly supported.
findings.evidence: code/sens_imbens.py benchmark_r2 (R2_D floor); runs/sens-imbens/metrics.json bench_black_r2d = 0, bench_married_r2d = 0, bench_nodegree_r2d = 0, strongest_robust_zero = black; claims.jsonl sens-reading; runs/NOTES.md 'Surprises'. Reviewer scratch check: V, V_-G and log-likelihood drops above. The fixed rule and its output stay. Remedy: the claim and paper say that the three 'robust' verdicts come from the floor (V_-G > V, because the index variance is dominated by CPS men far outside the treated range) and carry no information about race, marital status or degree as confounders. They do not write 'robust to a confounder as strong as race'. If the paper cites V and V_-G, they come from a logged run labelled as a post-results diagnostic (covariates and treatment only), not from my scratch numbers.
findings.response: Fixed: sens-reading and the black/married/nodegree bias claims now say these 'robust' verdicts come from flooring R2_D at zero (index variance dominated by CPS men outside the treated range) and carry no information about those confounders; no claim says 'robust to a confounder as strong as race'. V and V_-G are not cited (no logged run has them).

findings.text: Two claim texts omit qualifiers that the design requires next to the result. (a) disagree-trim says only 'not robust to control-only trimming', which reads as an overlap failure. design.method.control_only_trimming says rob-trim tests sensitivity to the nuisance models' training sample. The 8,125 dropped CPS men carry 0.09% of the control weight, and the cutoff rests on one treated man. rob-trim moves the estimate by 59 dollars, and its own repetitions range from 1,265 to 1,624, so the trigger is consistent with refitting noise. The abstract sentence is fixed and stays, but its meaning should be stated with it. (b) design.method.h3_placebo: 're75 is top-coded for CPS men (3,007 at the maximum) and not for NSW men; this is stated with the result'. placebo-effect and placebo-verdict do not state it, although placebo-re75 records cps_re75_at_max = 3007.
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl disagree-trim, placebo-effect, placebo-verdict; runs/rob-trim/metrics.json theta_rep0-4; runs/placebo-re75/metrics.json cps_re75_at_max; plan.json design.method.control_only_trimming and h3_placebo. Remedy: add one sentence to each claim text.
findings.response: Fixed: disagree-trim states what rob-trim tests (nuisance refit; dropped men carry 0.09% of control weight per the design's outcome-free computation; estimate moves 59; its repetitions 1,265-1,624, claims trim-theta-rep0-4); placebo-effect and placebo-verdict state the CPS re75 top-code (claim placebo-cps-re75-topcoded = 3,007 from the logged placebo run).

findings.text: The analysis runs used scripts that changed after code-r1 and were not re-reviewed. plan.json design.analysis_plan (code-review item) says 'a script changed after review is re-reviewed'. The PI brief 20261119T122759Z sent the Econometrician straight from the fixes to the runs. I have now read git diff 866903c..1d4682e on code/. The changes are exactly code-r1 F1-F4: the mbar_check tolerance and the stop in main_aipw, rob-trim's count report, convergence counts and the sens-imbens logit flags, the h2 gate guard, and the tests. Nothing touches the score, learners, bases, seeds, folds, clip or decision rules, and the unit-tests rerun (12:31-12:35Z) precedes main-aipw (12:35:36Z). So I find no effect on any number. The deviation from the approved plan is still undisclosed. I also confirm that code-r1 F1-F4 are fixed in the files; their status in reviews/code-r1 is still 'open'.
